exposure: Robson classification groups (based on obstetric characteristics like parity, previous caesarean section, onset of labor, gestational age, fetal lie)
cohort: The study analysed data from 179,463 women who gave birth in 56 referral-level facilities across Nigeria.
finding: The study found an overall caesarean section rate of 33%, with women with previous caesarean section (Robson Group 5) being the largest contributors, and particularly high rates in nulliparous and multiparous women without previous caesarean section (Robson Group 2 and 4), where pre-labour caesarean sections were common and labour induction rates were low.
mod_finding: The analysis highlights a high caesarean section rate overall, with previous caesarean section being the largest contributor, and also demonstrates high caesarean section rates in nulliparous and multiparous women without prior caesarean section, often due to pre-labour caesarean sections, alongside low rates of labour induction in these groups.
